question: Should OpenClaw add a plugin-visible skill install/update completion observer now, and what redacted payload plus observer-failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: Automation can prove the missing lifecycle surface, but choosing install metadata exposure, ordering, fail-open/fail-closed behavior, and scope across CLI/Gateway/UI is a security and product boundary decision.

options.title: Add minimal observer
options.body: Add a non-blocking completion hook with redacted source/provenance/outcome metadata, documented fail-open logging semantics, and tests across CLI/Gateway/UI install and update paths.

options.title: Keep blocking only
options.body: Declare `security.installPolicy` and `before_install` sufficient for install security, then close or split the audit-observer request as not planned.

options.title: Defer to ClawHub trust design
options.body: Hold the observer until maintainers define a broader ClawHub trust/provenance API that can provide the same audit events safely.

recommendation.title: Add minimal observer
recommendation.body: Add a non-blocking completion hook with redacted source/provenance/outcome metadata, documented fail-open logging semantics, and tests across CLI/Gateway/UI install and update paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across native ClawHub install behavior, security-gate alignment, and Gateway/UI install surfaces.
